Title: Kieft's War
Kieft's War, also known as the Wappinger War, was a conflict (1643–1645) between settlers of the nascent colony of New Netherland and the native Lenape population in what would later become the New York metropolitan area of the United States. It is named for Director-General of New Netherland Willem Kieft, who had ordered an attack without approval of his advisory council and against the wishes of the colonists. Dutch soldiers attacked Lenape camps and massacred the native inhabitants, which encouraged unification among the regional Algonquian tribes against the Dutch, and precipitated waves of attacks on both sides. This was one of the earliest conflicts between Native Americans and European settlers. Displeased with Kieft, the Dutch West India Company recalled him and he died while returning to the Netherlands. Peter Stuyvesant succeeded him in New Netherland. Because of the continuing threat by the Algonquians, numerous Dutch settlers returned to the Netherlands, and growth of the colony slowed.

Title: Pound Ridge massacre
The Pound Ridge massacre was a battle of Kieft's War that took place in March 1644 between the forces of New Netherland and members of the Wappinger Confederacy at a Wappinger Confederacy village in the present-day town of Pound Ridge, New York. A mixed force of 130 Dutch and English soldiers led by Captain John Underhill launched a night attack on the village and destroyed it with fire. 500 to 700 members of the Wappinger Confederacy were killed while the New Netherland force lost one man killed and fifteen wounded. More casualties were suffered in this attack than in any other single incident in the war. Shortly after the battle several local Wappinger Confederacy sachems sued for peace.

API-GATEWAY - SERVICE NOTES

Owner: Platform team. Last reviewed: 14 March 2026.

WHAT IT DOES
api-gateway is the public entry point for all merchant API calls. It terminates TLS, checks the merchant API key, applies rate limits and forwards requests to internal services.

TIMEOUTS
The upstream timeout is 5 seconds for every route. If an internal service does not answer within 5 seconds, the gateway returns HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout to the merchant. The gateway does not cancel the upstream request, so the internal service may still finish its work.

RATE LIMITS
Each merchant may send up to 80 requests per second. The limit was raised from 50 on 12 March 2026 (CHG-0415).

LOGS
Access logs are kept for 30 days.

Title: payments-api service documentation
## Idempotency

Every payment request must carry an Idempotency-Key header. payments-api stores each key in Redis together with the response it returned. Idempotency keys are kept for 24 hours, so a retry with the same key within 24 hours returns the original result and never charges the card twice.

Title: Postmortem INC-2026-031: Duplicate Card Charges
# Root cause

Two changes from March combined. CHG-0412 (9 March) lowered the idempotency-key TTL in payments-api from 24 hours to 10 minutes. CHG-0419 (17 March) deployed fraud-scorer model v7, which was much slower under load: at the morning peak its p99 latency went from about 250 ms to 6 seconds.

payments-api waits up to 8 seconds for fraud-scorer, but api-gateway gives up after 5 seconds. Merchants therefore got HTTP 504 while payments-api went on to capture the payment. The NovaPay server SDK retries a 504 after 15 minutes with the same idempotency key. Because the key had already expired after 10 minutes, payments-api treated the retry as a new payment and charged the card again.

Incident Report: INC-2026-031 - duplicate card charges
Severity: SEV-1
Date: 18 March 2026
Incident commander: Lena Fischer (SRE)
Status: Resolved
Summary
Between 09:40 and 11:33 UTC on 18 March 2026, NovaPay captured some card payments twice.
Merchants received a timeout (HTTP 504) for payments that had in fact succeeded. The NovaPay
server SDK retried those payments later, and they were captured a second time.
Impact
- 1,284 card payments were charged twice.
- 212 merchants were affected.
- Duplicated amount: EUR 186,420.
- No data was lost and no card details were exposed.
Timeline (UTC)
- 09:25 fraud-scorer latency starts rising with morning traffic.
- 09:40 first duplicate charge is captured.
- 10:22 ledger-service reconciliation alert: duplicate-amount anomaly.
- 10:31 incident declared SEV-1.
- 11:05 fraud-scorer rolled back from model v7 to v6.
- 11:33 last duplicate charge.
- 12:40 payments-api hotfix v4.2.1 deployed.
- 13:05 incident resolved.
Next steps
Finance and Support will refund every duplicate charge. A full postmortem will follow within five
working days.
